newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open unchanged, FOMC meeting awaited.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open unchanged, FOMC meeting awaited.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries opened unchanged in stagnant trade on Monday as investors waited for the decision of the Federal Reserve policy meeting set for Tuesday.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond opened at 96-15/32, yielding 6.91 percent, unchanged from Friday.
Five-year notes opened at 100-10/32, unchanged from Friday, yielding 6.55 percent. Two-year notes opened unchanged at 100-7/32, yielding 6.25 percent.

The Fed's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet on Tuesday and the prominent issue on the agenda as far as the market is concerned is whether the policymakers will vote to raise the key Federal funds rate another 25 basis points.

Economists say the outcome of the meeting is a close call. They say some recent data, such as a decline in April retail sales, continued very favorable trends in wholesale prices and subdued first-quarter employment costs mean that any need on the part of the central bank to strike a pre-emptive blow against inflation is less urgent.

The quiet early trade followed quiet overnight activity. Overseas investors are also doing no more than adjust positions before the FOMC monetary policy meeting on Tuesday, analysts said. Many European countries were on holiday.
"There's no major data or speeches on the calendar," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A.
The "center of gravity" for the June T-bond contract is 110-05, the 200-day moving average, he said.
"We've traded above it and below it," he said. "That should be the center of gravity for the market until we get the Fed's decision in.
"Investors would rather wait and see what the Fed is going to do before changing their stance," said Stiles.
Analysts said the Treasury market would keep an eye on the dollar's performance in the foreign exchange market and also on the CRB index of commodity prices.
"There is some interest in the dollar, but the dollar seems to have stabilized here," he said.
The dollar opened higher -- above 116 yen and 1.70 marks -- reflecting short-covering ahead of Tuesday's FOMC meeting.
The CRB index, which has risen lately due to higher copper and oil prices, was off 0.28 to 253.41.
Stiles said if the Fed leaves rates unchanged on Tuesday, the yield curve could steepen and the market would "try to go higher and fail."
If the Fed does raise rates, the yield curve would flatten with two-year maturities coming under more pressure than the long end, he said.

"There will be people stepping up to say the Fed has finished tightening cycle so let's buy it," said Stiles. "But be careful of those people. The issue is whether the economy is decelerating and that's still very much an open question."
At the short end of the maturity range, three-, six-month and year-bill rates were each up one basis point to 5.07 percent, 5.36 percent and 5.54 percent, respectively.
Ten-year notes were up 1/32 to 99-16/32, yielding 6.69 percent.
